title: Rule on Employer Benefit Charging Positions per Claim
content:
**1. Positions are held claim by claim.** Under Employer Benefit Charging, an employer holds one chargeable position on each claim for which it is a base-period employer, so the number of positions per employer is not capped. An employer charged on several claims holds as many positions as there are such claims; there is no maximum number of positions for one employer.

**2. One position per employer account and claim.** A position is opened only once per employer account and claim. Whether a position already exists is judged from the Department's records of positions, matched on the employer's tax account and the claim, never from the caller's account of it. A position on that account and claim in any status — noticed, responded, chargeable, protest pending, relieved or closed — means no second position is opened for that pair.

**3. Noncharged programs and later claims.** A claim under a program in the noncharged list opens no position. A later claim of the same claimant is a new claim with new positions.

## Points of judgement

| Situation (hypothetical) | Result under this rule |
|---|---|
| An employer is a base-period employer on three different claims | Three positions, one per claim |
| The same employer account and claim already show a closed position | No second position on that claim |
| A claimant files a new claim after an earlier claim | The new claim opens new positions for its base-period employers |
| The claim is under a program in the noncharged list | No position is opened |

**Basis Q&A.** *Does the size of an employer's workforce or its number of claims limit how many Employer Benefit Charging positions it can hold?* No. The only limit is one position per employer account and claim.
